Chapter 7: The Ongoing Work of Healing
Healing isn’t some neat, straight line. Honestly, it’s more like a winding path—sometimes you’re climbing uphill, sometimes you’re just trying to catch your breath. There are moments when you feel the weight of the past starting to lift, and hope feels... well, possible. And then there are days when old wounds crack open again, and the pain you thought you’d put behind you suddenly feels just as fresh as ever.
Therapy, for many, becomes this steady companion on the journey. Imagine sitting in a quiet space, finally letting out memories that have been locked away for years. It’s exhausting, sure—sometimes it feels like you’re digging through layers and layers of earth, searching for something precious hidden deep down. But every session, just a little more light manages to break through.
And there are breakthroughs. That moment when you see an old problem in a totally new way, and something inside you shifts. Maybe one day, while talking through a painful memory, you realize the shame you’ve been carrying didn’t belong to you at all—it belonged to the person who caused harm. That shift? It’s powerful. Suddenly, you can let go of a burden that was never meant for you.
But here’s something important: healing isn’t just about looking back. It’s also about learning how to live well now. That means building habits that actually support you—getting enough sleep, eating food that nourishes your body, moving around, and making time for things that make you smile. It also means learning to spot your triggers, and knowing when you need to pause, take a deep breath, and steady yourself when anxiety creeps in.
And let’s not forget the role of community. Finding people who truly understand what you’re going through—whether it’s a support group, a faith community, or a close friend—can make all the difference. There’s something comforting about hearing someone say, “Me too.” It reminds you that you’re not alone, and that others have walked this road and found ways to thrive.
Most folks don’t realize just how much work healing takes. It’s not only about surviving what happened, but about creating a life that feels new—one grounded in self-compassion, resilience, and hope. Are there setbacks? Of course. Sometimes, those old patterns feel impossible to break. But every time, you make that choice to keep moving forward, to believe—just for today—that healing really is possible, even when it feels far away.
Over time, the pain loses its grip. The memories might still be there, but they don’t control your present anymore. Instead, they become just one part of a bigger story—a story about survival, about growth, and about the ongoing, courageous work of becoming whole.
